body.zh-Hant: 1901年4月29日出生，後世稱昭和天皇；1921年因其父（後稱大正天皇）精神狀況，被任命為攝政，代行父親職務。
body.en: Born on 29 April 1901 and posthumously known as Shōwa; in 1921, because his father (later Emperor Taishō) was suffering from mental illness, he was appointed Prince Regent and took over his father's duties.

citations.quote: born in 1901 and posthumously known as Shōwa
in 1921 to the appointment of Hirohito as Prince Regent
was demonstrating erratic behavior, a result of mental illness
assuming the duties of his father

heading.en: Accession and end of the war

body.zh-Hant: 1926年12月25日大正天皇崩御，裕仁隨即繼位，改元昭和；1936年他迅速出面制止未遂的軍事政變（二二六事件）；1945年8月在兩顆原子彈投下後，他才果斷介入、促成停戰。
body.en: Emperor Taishō died on 25 December 1926 and Hirohito succeeded immediately, beginning the Shōwa era; he moved swiftly to halt the attempted military coup of 1936 (the Ni Ni Roku incident); in August 1945, after two atomic bombs were dropped, he decisively moved to stop the war.

In August, 1945, after two atomic bombs had been dropped on Japan

body.zh-Hant: 東條英機生於1884年（明治17年），出身岩手，1948年（昭和23年）去世，官至陸軍大將；曾任關東軍參謀長、陸軍次官、陸軍大臣，1941年10月以陸軍大臣身分兼任首相。
body.en: Tōjō Hideki was born in 1884 (Meiji 17) with Iwate given as his home prefecture and died in 1948; he was an army general who served as chief of staff of the Kwantung Army, vice-minister of the army and army minister, and in October 1941 became prime minister while remaining army minister.

body.zh-Hant: 1887年10月31日出生；1918年受召到廣州加入孫中山的新政府，1923年率團訪問蘇聯。
body.en: Born 31 October 1887; in 1918 he was summoned to join Sun Yat-sen's new government in Canton, and in 1923 he headed a group that visited the Soviet Union.

citations.quote: 1918, Chiang received a summons to join Sun in his new government in Canton
In 1923, he headed a group that visited the Soviet Union

body.zh-Hant: 1924年被任命為黃埔軍校校長；1926年被任命為國民革命軍總司令並發動北伐；1927年初北伐軍攻佔南京、上海，他在南京另立政府；北伐於1928年底攻佔北京而告終。
body.en: In 1924 he was appointed commandant of the Whampoa Military Academy; in 1926 he was appointed commander in chief of the National Revolutionary Army and launched the Northern Expedition; his troops captured Nanjing and Shanghai in early 1927, and he established a rival government in Nanjing; the expedition ended with the capture of Beijing at the end of 1928.

citations.quote: In 1924, Chiang was appointed commandant of the Whampoa Military Academy
appointed commander in chief of the National Revolutionary Army in 1926
and launched the Northern Expedition to unify China under the Kuomintang
captured Nanjing and Shanghai in early 1927
established a rival government in Nanjing
The Northern Expedition ended in triumph with the capture of Beijing
at the end of 1928

body.zh-Hant: 1948年由新國民大會依憲法選為總統，任職至1975年4月5日去世。
body.en: He was elected president by a new National Assembly under the constitution in 1948 and served as president until his death on 5 April 1975.

by a new National Assembly under the terms of the constitution in 1948

body.zh-Hant: 1870年4月22日出生；1895年出國，名義上為健康因素；同年底返回聖彼得堡後被警方逮捕。
body.en: Born 22 April 1870; in 1895 he went abroad, ostensibly for health reasons; on his return to St. Petersburg late in 1895 he was arrested by the police.

citations.quote: In 1895, he went abroad, ostensibly for health reasons
On his return to St. Petersburg late in 1895
only to be arrested by the police

heading.zh-Hant: 十月革命與人民委員會

body.zh-Hant: 1917年11月6至7日夜間發生世界上第一場成功的工人革命，國家領導權落入選舉產生的執行機構人民委員會手中，列寧擔任主席。
body.en: On the night of 6–7 November 1917 the world's first successful workers' revolution took place, and leadership of the country passed to an elected executive board, the Council of People's Commissars, with Lenin as chair.

citations.quote: As Russia sank further into anarchy during 1917
the night of November 6-7 the world’s first successful workers’ revolution
Leadership of the country passed into the hands of an elected executive board
the Council of People’s Commissars, with Lenin as chair

body.zh-Hant: 1922年初他首次中風，同年稍後再度中風，病情加重；1924年1月21日去世。
body.en: He suffered his first stroke in early 1922 and a second, more debilitating one later that year; he died on 21 January 1924.

body.zh-Hant: 1859年1月27日出生於柏林，屬霍亨索倫家族，父為腓特烈三世；1888年起任德意志皇帝兼普魯士國王。
body.en: Born in Berlin on 27 January 1859 into the Hohenzollern family, son of Frederick III; German Emperor and King of Prussia from 1888.

heading.en: Daily Telegraph affair and the eve of war

body.zh-Hant: 1908年爆發他統治期間最嚴重的危機「每日電訊報事件」；1914年7月，他最終屈服於軍事顧問的壓力，既未推動也未阻止第一次世界大戰的爆發。
body.en: The "Daily Telegraph affair" of 1908 was the most serious crisis of his reign; in July 1914 he finally yielded to the pressure of his military advisers, neither promoting nor preventing the outbreak of the First World War.

citations.quote: die schwerste Krise in seiner Herrschaft, die „Daily Telegraph-Affäre“ 1908
so unterwarf er sich im Juli 1914 schließlich dem Druck
dem Druck seiner militärischen Ratgeber
Weder beförderte W. den Beginn des 1. Weltkriegs noch verhinderte er ihn.

body.zh-Hant: 他身為陸海軍最高統帥；1918年11月28日正式退位，流亡二十一年，先在阿默龍恩城堡，1920年起住在多倫之家，1941年6月4日在多倫去世。
body.en: He was supreme commander of army and navy; he formally abdicated on 28 November 1918 and spent 21 years in exile, first at Amerongen castle and from 1920 at Haus Doorn, where he died on 4 June 1941.
